summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and recent gastrointestinal bleeding was transferred from rehab due to worsening weakness, shortness of breath, and right-sided chest and ear pain. He was found to have HCAP pneumonia with progression of right lung consolidations and a new left pleural effusion, treated with intravenous vancomycin and cefepime, later transitioned to oral doxycycline. Imaging also revealed acute on chronic sinusitis and right otitis media with tympanic membrane perforation, managed with ear drops, nasal sprays, and saline rinses. Hyponatremia and anemia were stable, and heart failure was managed without diuretic escalation. He improved clinically, remained euvolemic, and was discharged back to extended care with a plan to complete antibiotics and follow-up on sinus and pulmonary findings.
